elaine (sec-eng): SIEM flagged a sudden spike in decrypt operations against a prod-managed key used by service-account-prod-app in two regions. alert id: SIEM-1771234567. seeing ~120 decrypts in 10m (baseline ~2-5).
raj (oncall): Acknowledged. I'm querying KMS audit exports and listing recent IAM changes. Running: `gcloud logging read 'resource.type=cloud_kms_crypto_key' --freshness=1h` and `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=service-account-prod-app@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.
mike (infra): I pulled the KMS audit bucket. decrypt RPCs originate from two autoscaling groups and one external IP in eu-west-2 that we don't recognize. The SA key was created 3 months ago, last used yesterday. snippet: `protoPayload.methodName: "google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"`
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-177123 - potential exfil via key use. Severity: P2.
raj (oncall): For containment, recommend: 1) disable the service account key (not the SA). 2) rotate the key version used for encryption. 3) freeze affected VM instances in eu-west-2 and capture disk. Anyone object?
elaine (sec-eng): Agree. Also add a deny policy to block Decrypt for that SA on that key until we confirm. I'll prepare the IAM deny.
mike (infra): Commands I'll run now (dry-run then apply):
```
# disable key version
gcloud kms keys versions destroy 3 --key=projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/data/cryptoKeys/prod-k
# disable SA key
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete 0123456789abcdef --iam-account=service-account-prod-app@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
elaine (sec-eng): Collecting indicators: list of affected ciphertexts, decrypt call timestamps, calling VM instances, and the unknown IPs. We'll add to the incident DB.
sre-oncall: Noted, I'll throttle batches hitting the KMS endpoint to reduce blast radius and monitor latency impact.
lina (legal): Heads up from legal: keep all communications internal until we know customer impact. If customers are affected, we need to route through me for wording and escalation.
nate (cto): I'm preparing an exec one-pager. Key asks: scope, customer impact (yes/no), containment steps, timeline, and next steps. Share drafts here.
elaine (sec-eng): Quick status update: disabled SA key and added deny-binding for that SA on the specific CryptoKey. Rotating key version now. Preserving logs and snapshots.
raj (oncall): We've isolated decrypts to a single key version and a set of ephemeral instances. No evidence yet of plaintext exfiltration from object storage. Still investigating application logs for copied plaintext.
elaine (sec-eng): Drafting internal advisory for product, support, and legal. Will include FAQ and escalation path. Posting draft customer-facing notice for Lina to review: 
```
Customer notification (DRAFT):
We detected unusual activity involving access attempts to an encryption key used by some internal background services. We have contained the activity, rotated the affected key, and are continuing our investigation. At this time, we have no evidence that customer data was accessed. We will notify you promptly if our investigation indicates any impact.
```

lina (legal): Suggest tightening: remove "background services" -> specify "internal background processing service"; add expected follow-up timeline (24-72 hours) and point to contact (security@redwood.com). Also do not say "no evidence" without qualifiers: use "no evidence to date".
elaine (sec-eng): Updated draft per Lina. Also prepared an exec note (short):
```
Exec update (DRAFT):
- Detection: spike in KMS Decrypts for prod key KID:projects/.../cryptoKeys/prod-k, seen in us-west1 and eu-west-2.
- Impact: No confirmed customer data access to date. Potentially limited to internal plaintext used by background workloads.
- Containment: Disabled compromised SA key, applied IAM deny, rotated key version, froze suspicious instances.
- Next steps: Forensics (24h), customer impact assessment (48-72h), remediation plan (key rotation across workloads).
```
raj (oncall): For forensic notes: we need the VM disk snapshots, memory captures if possible, and the process list around relevant timestamps. Requesting SRE for snapshot ops.
sre-oncall: On it. Will attach snapshot ops ticket and ETA ~30m.
mike (infra): We should check our KMS integration with third-party CI/CD (deploy pipelines). I found an OAuth token used by a bot account that has also used the SA recently. Could be credential theft.
elaine (sec-eng): Adding CI/CD bot account to the scope. Please collect pipeline run metadata for the last 7 days.
nate (cto): Good work. Keep execs updated every 2 hours. If this escalates to P1, we switch to war room.
lina (legal): I'll draft press/customer comm if needed. Please do not send any external notifications until I sign off.
customer-comm: (automated) Created a secure draft in shared drive: https://drive.internal/redwood/sec/inc-177123. Lina please review 1st.
elaine (sec-eng): Post-incident actions list (initial):
- Full key rotation plan and timeline (owners: infra, sec)
- RBAC review for service accounts (owners: sec, infra, devex)
- Audit log retention policy check and improvement
- KMS integration hardening (limit decrypts to known IPs / VPCs)
- Run vulnerability scan on build artifacts referenced by bot account
- After-action report in 72h

raj (oncall): Closing loop: containment steps completed. Continuing evidence collection and customer impact assessment. Will update thread with any confirmed findings.
elaine (sec-eng): Thanks team. If anyone sees suspicious activity elsewhere, ping me and tag @incident-bot. :white_check_mark:
